plants.name: Wisteria sinensis
plants.description: A vigorous woody climbing vine that produces dramatic pendulous clusters of fragrant, pea-like flowers before or as its leaves emerge. Widely trained over pergolas, arbors, and walls in gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-spring to early summer (April to May in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to China; widely cultivated in temperate regions of Europe, North America, and East Asia
plants.funFact: Wisteria vines can live for over a century and some specimens, like one in Sierra Madre, California, cover more than an acre. Chinese wisteria twines counterclockwise, while Japanese wisteria twines clockwise.

plants.name: Syringa vulgaris
plants.description: A deciduous shrub that bears dense, cone-shaped clusters of intensely fragrant flowers. It thrives in regions with cold winters and is a classic cottage garden favorite.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late April to May in cool temperate Northern Hemisphere regions
plants.location: Native to the Balkan Peninsula; cultivated across northern Europe, the northeastern United States, and Canada
plants.funFact: Lilacs belong to the olive family (Oleaceae), and the flowers are edible, with a floral, slightly citrusy taste that is sometimes used in syrups and baked goods.

plants.name: Cornus florida
plants.description: A small deciduous understory tree whose showy 'flowers' are actually four large white or pink bracts surrounding a cluster of tiny greenish-yellow true flowers. It lights up woodland edges in spring.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-April to mid-May, peaking around late April in the southeastern and mid-Atlantic United States
plants.location: Eastern North America, from southern Ontario to Florida and west to eastern Texas
plants.funFact: The bright red fruits of the dogwood are an important food source for songbirds, and the tree is the state tree of Virginia and Missouri and the state flower of Virginia and North Carolina.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: Not in peak bloom in April in most of the world, so this entry highlights a different Southern Hemisphere autumn bloomer: this species is replaced here by Nerine's relative below.

plants.name: Nerine sarniensis
plants.description: A bulbous perennial that produces umbels of shimmering, wavy-petaled flowers on bare stalks. In the Southern Hemisphere it flowers in the autumn season, while the foliage emerges afterward.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn (March to May in the Southern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to the Western Cape of South Africa; grown in Mediterranean-climate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: The petals have a glittering, jewel-like sheen due to specialized epidermal cells, which gives the flowers a sparkling look in sunlight.
